supporting_observations.claim: The observed periodic HTTPS activity is consistent with the approved PixelForge updater: pfupdater.exe initiated proxy connections to updates.pixelforge-suite.com at roughly five-minute intervals, with one authentication-required response and other successful tunnels.
A Dropbox updater executable ran as SYSTEM from the workstation’s Program Files (x86) Dropbox directory. Dropbox is not among the approved services listed in the environment context.
A DNS query for x7k9m2.akamaized.net occurred shortly after DropboxUpdate.exe ran, but the available records do not associate that query with DropboxUpdate.exe.

A successful network logon to WS-SOKAFOR-01 used sam.okafor credentials and identified WS-LMARTINS-01 as the source. Since sam.okafor is the only IT administrator and remote administration is specified as originating only from WS-SOKAFOR-01, this warrants investigation; the records do not establish the purpose of the logon.

FILE-NWD-01 made an RPC endpoint-mapper connection to WS-LMARTINS-01. The inventory describes workstation patching as being initiated from WS-SOKAFOR-01, but these records do not identify the purpose or authenticated user for this connection.

known_telemetry_limitations: Winsec and Sysmon collection was unavailable for WS-NBLAKE-01 from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC, limiting organization-wide correlation during part of the review window.
The proxy records show CONNECT destinations, status, and tunnel metadata; the supplied evidence does not expose the contents of the HTTPS sessions.
The supplied records do not show the process or authenticated-user context on FILE-NWD-01 for its RPC connection to WS-LMARTINS-01.
claims_not_established: The periodic PixelForge updater connections are not shown to be malicious, and the records do not establish that they account for every connection described by the alert.
The evidence does not establish that DropboxUpdate.exe made an outbound connection, that the Akamai DNS query was caused by Dropbox, or that data was transferred to a file-sharing service.
The evidence does not establish whether sam.okafor credentials were used legitimately or without authorization, or what actions followed the network logon.
The evidence does not establish why FILE-NWD-01 connected to the workstation or whether that connection resulted in remote execution or other changes.
additional_evidence_needed: Confirm with IT whether Dropbox was authorized or installed on WS-LMARTINS-01; collect its binary hash, signature, installation history, and related service configuration.
Correlate the x7k9m2.akamaized.net DNS query with endpoint process telemetry and proxy or TLS records, if available.
Investigate the sam.okafor network logon using endpoint activity on WS-LMARTINS-01 and WS-SOKAFOR-01, including credential-use context and any resulting administrative actions.
Collect FILE-NWD-01 process, authentication, and remote-management records around 13:31 UTC to determine the purpose and outcome of its RPC connection.
Review proxy and endpoint connection records for the complete alert interval to confirm which process generated each outbound HTTPS connection.
